item.title: On the Geometric Structure of Hyperbolic Clifford Bundles and Associated Spin Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.03886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present the spinor structure associated with the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra of a real $n$-dimensional vector space $V$, which is denoted by $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$. Unlike the standard Clifford algebra, the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathcal{C}l(H_V)$ simultaneously accommodates both multiforms and multivectors in a single algebraic structure, making it the natural framework---known as the ``mother algebra''---for the study of superfields in theoretical physics and for generalizing the Clifford bundle formalism to hyperbolic structures arising in gravitational theories. The orthogonal groups and orthogonal transformations associated to the hyperbolic space $H_{V}$ are presented. The Clifford--Lipschitz group and the Pin and Spin groups associated with $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$ are defined. Then, the frame bundle and spinor structure associated to Hyperbolic Clifford algebra is derived.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Notte-Cuello

item.title: A hybrid quantum-classical lattice kinetic scheme with tensor-train feedback for incompressible flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.04500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear lattice kinetic simulation requires each updated distribution to supply the velocity and gradients that determine the next step. In a quantum-classical solver, reading out the full distribution incurs work proportional to the lattice size. We construct a tensor-train (TT) interface that retains reusable classical cores at the physical amplitude scale for a full-relaxation lattice kinetic scheme. The cores supply nonlinear coefficients and prepare each quantum input. Energy-scaled propagation and coordinate recovery encode the updated distribution, and alternating least-squares reconstruction converts signed Hadamard-test overlaps into output cores by restoring a known normalization factor. The next step starts from accepted cores without replaying previous quantum evolution. Under positive, unit-sum reference coefficients, positive lower and finite upper density bounds, and Lipschitz equilibrium sensitivity, perturbation bounds relate local defects to feedback errors. Resource bounds account for classical operations, circuit execution, sampling, and verification. Classical diagnostics expose why distribution accuracy alone is insufficient: in 80-step feedback on a $16\times16$ grid, rank cap 4 nearly eliminates the vortex despite a final distribution error below $1\%$, whereas rank cap 12 gives relative velocity error $1.03\times10^{-3}$. Four-step binomial readout simulations show that tightening core sampling tolerance threefold raises the prescribed sufficient budget from $5.97\times10^{12}$ to $5.37\times10^{13}$ shots as the result approaches the fixed-rank, fixed-sweep exact-overlap trajectory. The interface therefore provides a way to connect quantum propagation to nonlinear feedback and to assess the separate demands of compression, velocity accuracy, and readout precision.
item.dc:creator: Yongwei Guo, Yuan Yu, Yue Yu, Yuting Zhou

item.title: Eigenstates on $O^\ast$-algebras with an application to ladder operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.04550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following some recent results, we consider here a particular class of states on a $O^\ast$-algebra $\M$ which we call {\em eigenstates of an element} $A\in\M$, and we deduce some of their properties. Then, we apply our definition to a family of ladder elements, i.e. elements of $\M$ obeying certain algebraic (commutation) relations which are physically motivated, and we discuss several results for these states
item.dc:creator: Fabio Bagarello, Hiroshi Inoue, Salvatore Triolo

item.title: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.04613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. After reviewing the standard approach based on non-commutative harmonic analysis, we develop two complementary methods originating from the quantization of the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, both with and without a magnetic monopole field. The first is based on $\mathbf{SU}(n)$-equivariant first-order GLSM formulation and gives explicit eigenfunctions in terms of projectors and Pl\"ucker coordinates. The second uses a spin-chain realization of free particles on manifolds and describes the space of square-integrable functions, or sections in the magnetic case, through limiting tensor products of long rectangular $\mathbf{SU}(n)$ representations. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.
item.dc:creator: Dmitri Bykov, Viacheslav Krivorol

item.title: Lorentz-Invariant Measure for Path Integrals in the Future Cone
item.description: arXiv:2611.04669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a measure on continuous paths in the future cone of two-dimensional space that is invariant under the orthochronous Lorentz group and quasi-invariant under the action of the diffeomorphism group. We use the proposed measure to obtain the fundamental solution of the heat equation. The result agrees with the expression obtained by other methods.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir V. Belokurov, Vsevolod V. Chistiakov, Klavdiia A. Lursmanashvili, Evgeniy T. Shavgulidze

item.title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutionsin 5+1 dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $\lambda=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction in terms of the profile.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Bizo\'n

item.title: Multiplicity and parity in Hirota's $N$-soliton conditions: the bilinear families $L\,(D_x^{3}+\Lambda)^{2n+1}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hirota's three-soliton condition is the standard test for the integrability of a bilinear equation $P(D)f\cdot f=0$, and the folklore implication ``three-soliton condition $\Rightarrow$ $N$-soliton solutions for all $N$'' underlies the classifications of Hietarinta. We study this implication in two directions. The first is the family $L\,(D_x^3+\Lambda)^{2n+1}f\cdot f=0$ with $L$, $\Lambda$ linear forms in the Hirota operators, which for $n=0$ contains the Korteweg--de Vries, Ito and Boiti--Leon--Manna--Pempinelli equations and for $L=D_x$ is the family of G\"urses and Pekcan. On the principal component of the dispersion variety the $N$-soliton condition reduces to a sign sum of two bialternants; counting odd exponents shows that for $n=0$ the class is Hirota integrable and that for $n\ge1$ the three-soliton condition holds for every $L$, and an explicit formula for the four-soliton residual proves the G\"urses--Pekcan conjecture that the four-soliton condition fails for every $n\ge1$. The formula yields sum-of-squares certificates excluding four-soliton solutions at every real configuration for the G\"urses--Pekcan and Ito equations, classifies the real members of the class, and determines maximal numbers of nondegenerate solitons: exactly four or five for $n=1$ according as $L$ lies in the span of $D_x,\Lambda$ or not, five for $n=2$ and $L=D_x$, and finite for every $n\ge1$ and every $L$. The second direction is a reformulation of the implication for a single non-hyperplane component of multiplicity one, which we prove, with complete classifications, for all graph-type dispersions $L(q(D)+D_t)$, for every irreducible even quadric component in any dimension and with an arbitrary cofactor, for parabolic components, for the dispersions $F(\ell)+Q$ containing the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili surface, and, with a prescribed one-parameter phase family, for the cubic graph.
item.dc:creator: Shi Zhenhua

item.title: High-order compact ALE gas-kinetic scheme on three-dimensional unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) is developed for compressible arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) computations on three-dimensional unstructured meshes. To achieve high-order spatial accuracy, a large number of matrix inversions are required for spatial reconstruction. In ALE computations, the mesh moves and the geometric information must be recalculated at each time step, which reduces computational efficiency. To improve efficiency, a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy is employed to construct a quadratic polynomial on unstructured meshes. By differentiating the candidate polynomial, the quadratic terms are obtained by the least-squares method using the average gradient values of the cell itself and its neighboring cells. The linear terms of the polynomial are also determined by the least-squares method. On three-dimensional unstructured meshes, a $3\times3$ coefficient matrix must be stored, and four least-squares procedures are required to construct a quadratic polynomial. To suppress numerical oscillations in flows with discontinuities, generalized essentially non-oscillatory (GENO) reconstruction and a gradient compression factor are adopted. To accelerate the computation, a multi-GPU accelerated code is implemented using Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and Message Passing Interface (MPI). The current scheme is fully explicit, and the acceleration framework can be developed based on cell-level parallelism. Numerical examples are presented to evaluate the accuracy and robustness of the scheme, including flows with strong discontinuities, pitching wings, and helicopter rotors. Numerical results confirm the excellent performance of the compact ALE scheme on unstructured meshes.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Wang, Xing Ji, Liang Pan

item.title: Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
item.description: arXiv:2611.05186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Saberi, Muqtasid Tashfin, Andreas Vogel

item.title: Non-local approximations for the Schr\"odinger operator with a general point interaction via the non-relativistic limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.05210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the one-dimensional Dirac operator $D_{A,c}$ with a general, not necessarily self-adjoint, point interaction at the origin, whose strength is described by an arbitrary complex $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ and suitably rescaled by the speed of light $c$, together with its non-local approximations $D_{A,c}^{\epsilon}$ obtained by replacing the Dirac distribution by a rank-one projection onto a scaled function $v_\epsilon$. It is known that $D_{A,c}^\epsilon \to D_{A,c}$ as $\epsilon\to 0+$ and that $D_{A,c}-c^2/2$ converges, as $c\to+\infty$, to the Schr\"odinger operator $H_A$ with the general point interaction, both in the norm resolvent sense. We prove that the first convergence is uniform with respect to $c$ in a neighbourhood of $+\infty$, and we provide explicit rates of convergence. Combining this with an explicit computation of the non-relativistic limit of $D_{A,c}^\epsilon$ for fixed $\epsilon$, we show that the two limits can be interchanged and that the corresponding double limit exists. As a by-product we obtain a family of non-local, rank-two approximations $H_A^\epsilon$ of $H_A$ that converge to $H_A$ in the norm resolvent sense. Contrary to the relativistic setting, the coupling constants of $H_A^\epsilon$ are renormalized; we give an explicit formula for this renormalization.
item.dc:creator: Luk\'{a}\v{s} Heriban

item.title: Dynamical Properties of the Multiple Elastic Pendulum
item.description: arXiv:2611.05312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article studies the dynamical properties of the multiple elastic pendulum formed by an arbitrary number of point masses connected in a chain by elastic springs. First, using the Lagrangian formulation, the equations of motion governing the system's behavior, accounting for both large-angle displacements and elastic deformations, are derived. It is shown that well-established, low-dimensional systems, such as the classical double elastic pendulum, can be systematically recovered as particular cases directly from the general equations of motion after applying the appropriates particular conditions. The behavior of the system under small oscillations near its stable equilibrium is also investigated. For this case, the linearized equations allow the solution of the eigenvalue problem, demonstrating that in this case uncoupled behavior between the angular displacements and the spring elongations.
item.dc:creator: Luis Rozas

item.title: Bayesian BiLO: Bilevel Local Operator Learning for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification of Bayesian PDE Inverse Problems with Low-Rank Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2507.17019v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncertainty quantification in PDE inverse problems is essential in many applications. Scientific machine learning and AI enable data-driven learning of model components while preserving physical structure, and provide the scalability and adaptability needed for emerging imaging technologies and clinical insights. We develop a Bilevel Local Operator Learning framework for Bayesian inference in PDEs (B-BiLO). At the upper level, we sample parameters from the posterior via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, while at the lower level we fine-tune a neural network via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to approximate the solution operator locally. B-BiLO enables efficient gradient-based sampling without synthetic data or adjoint equations and avoids sampling in high-dimensional weight space, as in Bayesian neural networks, by optimizing weights deterministically. We analyze errors from approximate lower-level optimization and establish their impact on posterior accuracy. Numerical experiments across PDE models, including tumor growth, demonstrate that B-BiLO achieves accurate and efficient uncertainty quantification.
item.dc:creator: Ray Zirui Zhang, Christopher E. Miles, Xiaohui Xie, John S. Lowengrub

item.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.03857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Brollo

item.title: Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.04026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.
item.dc:creator: Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo

item.title: Schrodinger group along the horocycles and Egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.04131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study Egorov's theorem for Laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in Zelditch's quantization. In this quantization, the remainder in Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. Forward in time, we show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the Ehrenfest time T_E=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter. Backward in time, we introduce the Schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. We show that Egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -T_E+T_h for any Th going to infinity with 0<=T_h<=T_E. Moreover, the limit of the remainder in Egorov's theorem at the Ehrenfest time -T_E is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the Liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the Schrodinger group. Consequently, Egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -T_E (and in fact, at -T_E-T for any fixed T in R if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. Thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (QUE) conjecture is equivalent to this Egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. Furthermore, QUE holds with a polynomial rate if and only if Egorov's theorem holds at -T_E with a polynomial remainder. In this case, Egorov's theorem holds beyond -T_E with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in QUE, the longer the time is in Egorov's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Han

item.title: Feynman Propagators on Exponentially Decaying Perturbations of Stationary Spacetimes with Compact Cauchy Surface
item.description: arXiv:2611.04133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct Feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact Cauchy surface. The propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted Sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $\Gamma$. We then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of Dirac operators using a continuous Wick-like rotation to relate it to the Riemannian case.
item.dc:creator: Selim Amar

item.title: The Characteristic Initial Value Problem for the 3D Compressible Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove local existence and uniqueness, propagation of Sobolev regularity, and continuation criteria results for the characteristic initial value problem for the 3D compressible Euler equations. This is the Cauchy problem with initial data given on a pair of transversally intersecting (acoustically) null hypersurfaces. The region of existence in our main theorem is a future-neighborhood of the union of the data null hypersurfaces, where the size of the neighborhood depends on various norms of the data as well as the structure of the data null hypersurfaces. We allow for any equation of state with positive sound speed, and we do not make any symmetry, irrotationality, or isentropicity assumptions. Our analysis relies on the geometric formulation of the flow derived in [Speck19], which decomposes the equations into a "wave-part" coupled to a "transport-div-curl" part. Compared to Rendall's celebrated solution of the characteristic initial value problem for wave equations [Rendall90], substantial new ideas are needed to handle the fact that the compressible Euler equations are more complicated than pure wave equations.
item.dc:creator: Jared Speck, Sifan Yu

item.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Blasco

item.title: A note on the BRST-BV Formalism Explanation of Deformation Quantization and Algebraic Index Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we begin with considering the simple one-dimensional field theory describing a single free particle on manifold, and apply the BRST formalism and BV quantization to this model following the standard procedures in physics. Through calculations that, while not fully rigorous, have a more transparent physical interpretation, then subsequent geometric identifications, we recover the deformation quantization and algebraic index theorem on symplectic manifold. This note thus elucidates the physical origins and mechanisms of these mathematical results.
item.dc:creator: Lihao Zhao

item.title: Scaling laws for linear-elastic two-variant martensitic phase transitions in general domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.04329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a two-well problem within geometrically linear elasticity, on a bounded Lipschitz set in dimension $n\ge 2$. We assume that the two wells are compatible through a symmetrized rank-one connection and that the displacement matches their average on the boundary, and we include a regularization based on the total surface energy. We show that there are two distinct regimes, with the energy scaling differently in terms of the surface-energy coefficient $\eps$: it is proportional to $\eps^{2/3}$ if there are two distinct compatible twin-normal directions, and to $\eps^{4/5}$ if there is only one. This matches previous findings in rectangles and other special geometries, mostly in two dimensions, and the lower bounds obtained by a Fourier method by Rai\c{t}\u{a}, R\"uland, Tissot and Tribuzio (2024). Our results are obtained by explicit constructions, which contain a self-similar refinement of oscillations close to the boundary, and by a short real-space proof of the matching lower bounds.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Conti, Oleksandr Misiats

item.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.
item.dc:creator: Hesam Hosseini, Jinpei Zhao, Masahito Hayashi

item.title: Weak uniqueness and autonomous approximation for the SLE-reversible Weil-Petersson response diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.04417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the self-consistent common-noise equation associated with the Weil--Petersson response differential of the rotationally marked SLE welding probability. For $0<\kappa\leq4$, we prove joint weak uniqueness among continuous adapted weak solutions whose law at each deterministic time is the welding probability, and obtain the Markov property in the original filtration. A conditional Gaussian lift and capacity localization give the required $L^1$ generator-range density. Identification with the canonical law gives stationarity and reversibility. We also construct autonomous Fej\'er and Poisson regularizations with pathwise-unique global strong solutions. Their joint state-noise laws converge to the canonical law for every initial probability absolutely continuous with respect to the welding probability.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Uniqueness in an incompressible fluid with objective heat conduction model
item.description: arXiv:2611.04516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the context of heat conduction, the equations of Maxwell-Cattaneo is a successful alternative to the Fourier's law. In 2009, Christov proposed a frame-independent (or objective) generalization of Maxwell-Cattaneo equation. For a more general class of objective heat conduction Maxwell-Cattaneo-Christov equations proposed by Angeles, a uniqueness result is proved, applied to an incompressible fluid.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Kinza Arshad, Martina Nunziata & Vincenzo Tibullo (15 Apr 2025): Uniqueness in an incompressible fluid with objective heat conduction model, Journal of Thermal Stresses
item.dc:creator: Kinza Arshad, Martina Nunziata, Vincenzo Tibullo

item.title: Stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.04739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The aim of this article is to derive a stochastic interpretation of the Water Waves equations, based on the location uncertainty principle (LU). Next, these equations are used to infer simpler models from scaling limits, such as the Saint-Venant, Boussinesq and Serre-Green-Naghdi ones. Once adapted to the stochastic setting, these models have been successfully implemented numerically, and we show several experiments to assess their properties -- for example the breaking of the wave symmetry, and the influence of time correlated noises.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Moneyron (ODYSSEY, IRMAR)

item.title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2611.04791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Moreno D\'iaz, Juan B. Sancho de Salas

item.title: Exponential decay for the two-dimensional Heisenberg model
item.description: arXiv:2611.04908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we prove exponential decay for the spin correlation of the spin $O(\mathsf{N})$ model for $\mathsf{N}\geq3$ at every inverse temperature $ \beta>0 $. In particular, our work confirms Polyakov's prediction in 1975 on the Heisenberg model, i.e., the case of $\mathsf{N}=3$. To this end, we investigate a generalized $O(\mathsf{N})$ model where $ \mathsf{N} $ is a positive \emph{real number}, as follows: we sample a loop soup on the metric graph (say of a box) with intensity $ \tfrac{\mathsf{N}}{2} $ subject to the conditioning that the local time at each lattice vertex is $\beta$, and then for each loop we independently assign it to copies $1\leq \mathsf{i}\leq \lceil\mathsf{N}\rceil$ such that it is assigned to copy $\mathsf{i}$ with probability $ \tfrac{1}{\mathsf{N}} $ for $ 1\leq \mathsf{i}\leq \lfloor\mathsf{N}\rfloor $. Then, by Lupu's isomorphism theorem, we can construct a spin field by assigning a random sign to each loop soup cluster in each copy independently, such that the field coincides with the spin $O(\mathsf{N})$ model when $\mathsf{N}$ is an integer. We then establish exponential decay for every real-valued $\mathsf{N}>2$. Our result reveals an underlying mechanism for exponential decay, which emerges as soon as $\mathsf{N}>2$ (i.e., as soon as beyond the range of the XY model) and does not necessarily rely on the rotation symmetry in the sphere $ \mathbb{S}^{2} $.
item.dc:creator: Jian Ding, Fenglin Huang, Peng Yang

item.title: The Nonlinear Physics and Statistical Field Theory of Twilight Clouds: Hovering Dynamics and Dynamic Inertia Emergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.04924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Twilight clouds are small, optically faint warm clouds whose droplets fluctuate between haze and activated growth. We develop a nonequilibrium statistical field theory linking this regime to cloud-field organization through K\"ohler microphysics, supersaturation transport, and turbulent mixing. At parcel level, supersaturation rapidly tracks slow droplet growth with a finite lag. Mixing-induced supersaturation removal drives a saddle-node bifurcation, shifting the activation threshold and supporting intermittent hovering under turbulent fluctuations. Starting from turbulent transport of supersaturation coupled to droplet growth, we derive a droplet-supersaturation field system and formulate it within the Martin-Siggia-Rose framework. A Gurari-type variational reduction inspired by polaron theory eliminates the fast bath. Turbulence dresses the slow droplet field, shrinks the forbidden zone below the equilibrium curve, and raises the mixing threshold required to suppress activation. Each droplet population induces a screened supersaturation halo that couples neighboring cloud elements; its delayed adjustment generates dynamic inertia and temporally correlated noise. The resulting nonlinear, non-Markovian pseudoparabolic stochastic equation has a bounded frozen-background response at short wavelengths. Its long-wave coupling amplifies contrasts where the dressed slow manifold turns downward. Comparisons with the parent two-field system show that a spatially correlated Markovian closure preserves droplet-radius distributions and cloudlet organization. Near the activation fold, restoring residual-bath fluctuation memory improves recurrent-hovering frequency and patch extent without recalibrating the drift or fitting a correlation time. More broadly, the framework identifies how slow fields acquire interactions and inertia through the relaxing, diffusive environments they modify.
item.dc:creator: Micka\"el D. Chekroun, Ilan Koren

item.title: Almost primes in short intervals and averages of long Dirichlet polynomial approximations to $(\zeta'/\zeta)^{k}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.05000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the mean square of long truncations of the Dirichlet series for $\bigl(\zeta'/\zeta\bigr)^{k}$ on the critical line; we establish the connection between this problem and the short-interval variance of the convoluted von Mangoldt function $\Lambda^{*k}$ in short intervals and in arithmetic progressions. Under a shifted moments conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we prove that the short-interval variance leading coefficient is the derivative of the mean-square leading coefficient. A unitary trace-sum average governs the variance of sums of $\Lambda^{*k}$ over monic polynomials in $\mathbb F_q[T]$; we denote its leading coefficient by $\delta_k(c)$, where the total trace degree and matrix size grow with a fixed ratio $c$. Under a weaker shifted moments conjecture and RH, we recover this $\delta_k(c)$ as the leading coefficient of the variance of short-interval sums of $\Lambda^{*k}$ over the integers. It is the counterpart of $\gamma_k(c)$, the piecewise polynomial from the variance of divisor sums, with the Dirichlet coefficients of $\zeta(s)^k$ replaced by those of $\bigl(-\zeta'/\zeta\bigr)^k$.
item.dc:creator: Siegfred Baluyot, John Brian Conrey, Ayesha Irfan, Nina C. Snaith

item.title: The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of G\'erard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum G\'erard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.
item.dc:creator: Marine De Clerck, Oleg Evnin

item.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the monochromatic three-arm exponent for critical planar percolation through the exact spectral threshold of an explicit positive integral operator family with elementary kernels, obtaining $\xi_3=0.76928375\cdots$. Unlike the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) event, the three-arm event can be obstructed by two distinct white clusters, so a Markovian exploration must retain the past connections. We introduce a two-point boundary observable that records these connections. Using the coupling between conformal loop ensemble (CLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG), this observable satisfies a renewal equation in terms of quantum boundary lengths, and yields the explicit operator whose spectral information determines $\xi_3$. Our approach also gives an explicit spectral characterization of monochromatic $n$-arm exponents for all $n\ge4$.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai

item.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the $O(N)$ Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on a spin system with $n$ sites and possibly infinite spin spaces. We prove local-to-global spectral-gap bounds for block Glauber dynamics. Given a symmetric, entrywise nonnegative matrix $A$ with zero diagonal and $\lambda_{\max}(A)<1$ encoding local spectral bounds for a spin system, we derive global spectral-gap bounds for block dynamics on its marginal distributions. These bounds are sharp: the Gaussian system with covariance $(I-A)^{-1}$ attains equality for every choice of disjoint blocks. Our proof extends the Bochner method through an abstract inequality for orthogonal projections on Hilbert spaces. As an application, we prove that Glauber dynamics for the $O(N)$ model, with $N\geq 2$, arbitrary external fields, and couplings of either sign, has spectral gap at least $(1-\|J_{\mathrm{abs}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}/N)/n$, where $J$ is the interaction matrix and $J_{\mathrm{abs}}=(|J_{ij}|)$. We also obtain spectral bounds for swap walks and local spectral expansion of partite simplicial complexes. For complexes formed from disjoint groups of ranks in random flags of subspaces over $\mathbb F_q$, we obtain a one-sided local spectral expansion bound of $2\sqrt q/(q+1)$. This bound is independent of the number and sizes of each group, and is nontrivial for every prime power $q$. Finally, for random forests $F$ of any finite graph with arbitrary positive edge weights, we prove that \[ \Pr(e,f\in F)\le \frac{4}{3} \Pr(e\in F)\Pr(f\in F) \] for distinct edges $e,f$, improving the factor 2 supplied by general log-concavity bounds for matroid independent sets. The argument combines our extended Bochner method with the analysis of an auxiliary real stable polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Leake, Anqi Li

item.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $\lambda_c$ from the classical value $2\pi r_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $\lambda_c<2\pi r_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $\lambda_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Khenner

item.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.05293v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $\rho$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2\pi\rho(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\rho} + o(\sqrt{\rho}))$ as $\rho \to 0$, and the condensate fraction $\eta$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $\eta = 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\rho} + o(\sqrt{\rho})$ as $\rho \to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,\chi_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed El Hedi Bahri, Ian Jauslin

item.title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05329v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrt{\pi}$.
item.dc:creator: Shu-Heng Shao, Nikita Sopenko

item.title: Uniform local smoothing for the derivative NLS and the soliton mass threshold
item.description: arXiv:2611.05330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Harrop-Griffiths, Killip, Ntekoume and Vi\c{s}an proved that the derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (DNLS) is globally well-posed in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. A key ingredient of their proof is a local smoothing estimate. It holds on $L^2$-equicontinuous sets of initial data, but it cannot hold on $L^2$-balls, because rescaled stationary solitons, all of mass $2\pi$, violate it. This raises a natural question: for which masses $m$ does local smoothing hold uniformly on the ball $\{M(q_0)\le m\}$? We prove three results. First, we give a quantitative version of the local smoothing estimate in which the data enter only through the mass and an explicit frequency scale $\kappa(q_0)$. On time intervals of length $2T$ the bound grows like $1+\kappa(q_0)^2T$, and the stationary soliton shows that the power of $\kappa$ cannot be lowered below one. Second, we prove uniform local smoothing on balls of small mass, together with a scale-invariant Morrey-type form and a localized $L^4_{t,x}$ bound. Third, we analyse the soliton family from both sides. The uniform constant must blow up at least like $(2\pi-m)^{-1}$ as $m\uparrow 2\pi$, while every soliton of mass $m<2\pi$ satisfies local smoothing with a constant $O((2\pi-m)^{-1})$. These facts single out the stationary-soliton mass $2\pi$, which is also the Hayashi--Ozawa coercivity threshold, as the natural candidate for the sharp threshold. We formulate this as a conjecture, give a spectral reformulation in terms of the Kaup--Newell scattering data, and discuss the obstacles to a proof.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05357v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $\alpha$ and Green function decay exponent $
u$. We prove that the probability that the cluster of a vertex reaches distance $R$ is of order $R^{- eta}$ when $2\alpha<3
u$, where $ eta=\alpha-
u$ is the walk dimension, and that the same holds up to a logarithmic factor in the upper bound when $2\alpha=3
u$. On $\mathbb Z^d$ these conditions read $d>6$ and $d=6$. The upper bound combines a general entropic bound, which compares the law of the cluster under the critical loop soup and under a massive one, with a Simon-Lieb-type inequality for the massive field derived from its Markov property. The arguments are robust and require no transitivity. The lower bound follows from a competition between the capacity and the volume of the cluster. In both bounds, the key quantity is the expected exit time of the random walk from balls, which links the volume of the cluster to its radius.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Rodriguez, Jialu Shi, Wen Zhang

item.title: Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
item.description: arXiv:2611.05378v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct boundary Liouville conformal field theory at central charge $c\leq1$ with FZZT-type boundary conditions and show that it satisfies the Cardy--Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and the annulus. Using the analytic bootstrap we derive the so far missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants and a consistent disk one-point function as explicit meromorphic functions of the Liouville momenta. In sharp contrast to $c\geq25$, the open-string spectrum between two ``timelike'' FZZT boundaries is \emph{discrete}, yet non-trivially consistent through open-closed duality with the \emph{continuous} closed-string spectrum of Ribault and Santachiara.
item.dc:creator: Panos Betzios, Paul Ghiringhelli, Olga Papadoulaki, Ioannis Tsiares

item.title: Magnetism and infrared divergence in a Hubbard-phonon interacting system
item.description: arXiv:1008.2056v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a finite Hubbard model coupled to a massless phonon field through a form factor common to all sites that satisfies the infrared singular condition. The Hamiltonian has no ground state in the Fock representation. With the unitary transformation of Arai and Hirokawa, the ground states with infrared cutoff define states on the Weyl algebra over the form domain of the inverse dispersion, and they converge to a ground state in a representation inequivalent to the Fock representation. In this representation the ground states are the products of the ground states of the Hubbard model and the phonon vacuum, so that the model has ferromagnetic or unique spin-singlet ground states according to the hopping matrix and the electron number.
item.dc:creator: Yoshitsugu Sekine

item.title: Phonon Bose-Einstein condensation in a Hubbard-phonon interacting system with infrared divergence
item.description: arXiv:1308.5589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the grand canonical Gibbs states of a finite Hubbard model coupled to massless phonons with the dispersion relation $|k|^s$, $1\leq s<d$, at finite temperature. We keep the decoupling setting of the zero-temperature analysis, in which the electron-phonon form factor is common to all sites. An explicit unitary transformation factorizes the Gibbs state into the electron Gibbs state and the free phonon Gibbs state up to a phase, and the phonons exhibit Bose-Einstein condensation in the thermodynamic limit with the critical density of the free Bose gas. Assuming the convergence of this phase as the infrared cutoff is removed, the condensed state is the mixture of mutually disjoint component states with broken gauge symmetry, described by their expectations on the Weyl algebra. Physically, phonons are considered not to undergo Bose-Einstein condensation arxiv:1207.4621, and the study of a mechanism that suppresses this mathematical and formal condensation is left for future research.
item.dc:creator: Yoshitsugu Sekine

item.title: Highest weight vectors, shifted topological recursion and quantum curves
item.description: arXiv:2412.09120v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the theory of topological recursion by considering Airy structures whose partition functions are highest weight vectors of particular $\mathcal{W}$-algebra representations. Such highest weight vectors arise as partition functions of Airy structures only under certain conditions on the representations. In the spectral curve formulation of topological recursion, we show that this generalization amounts to adding specific terms to the correlators $ \omega_{g,1}$, which leads to a ``shifted topological recursion'' formula. We then prove that the wave-functions constructed from this shifted version of topological recursion are WKB solutions of families of quantizations of the spectral curve with $ \hbar$-dependent terms. In the reverse direction, starting from an $\hbar$-connection, we find that it is of topological type if the exact same conditions that we found for the Airy structures are satisfied. When this happens, the resulting shifted loop equations can be solved by the shifted topological recursion obtained earlier.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Mathematical Physics, 406 (2025), no. 11, paper No. 274, 71 pp
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Belliard, Vincent Bouchard, Reinier Kramer, Tanner Nelson

item.title: Equilibrium-energy-scaled quantum lattice Boltzmann method for variable-velocity linear advection--diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2602.09799v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a quantum lattice Boltzmann method for linear advection--diffusion equations with prescribed space- and time-dependent velocities. Direct block-encoding can accumulate normalization factors that suppress success probability exponentially, even when the classical propagator remains bounded. We control this loss by scaling each distribution component by the inverse square root of its local equilibrium weight. For uniformly positive weights and dimensionless relaxation times $\tau^*\geq 1/2$, this equilibrium energy scaling gives the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook collision operator unit spectral norm while preserving the discrete dynamics. Streaming normalization depends on weight ratios at the departure and arrival positions and times of each step; these ratios equal one for uniform steady advection. For periodic streaming, cumulative normalization stays bounded under mesh refinement at fixed physical time if logarithmic derivatives of the weights along streaming trajectories are bounded uniformly in space, time, and mesh resolution. A single-step block-encoding with two flag qubits supports coherent propagation of the full kinetic distribution without intermediate measurements. We compare oracle query bounds for time marching with those for a history-state linear system built from the same scaled operator, under specified assumptions on initial-state preparation and coefficient access. Tests in one and two dimensions and noiseless circuit simulations verify the construction. In a controlled comparison after 50 steps, scaling increases the probability of preparing the quantum state encoding the terminal distribution by approximately $450\times$. Classical refinement diagnostics up to $N_t=16{,}384$ steps confirm bounded cumulative normalization. The scaling controls additional normalization losses while retaining physical diffusive attenuation.
item.dc:creator: Yuan He, Yuan Yu, Yue Yu, Yuting Zhou

item.title: Notes on obstructions in the hyperbolic Clifford algebra bundle structure
item.description: arXiv:2605.16558v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Starting from a general analysis of obstruction classes, we develop the investigation of obstructions associated with the bundle structure of the hyperbolic Clifford algebra. By taking into account particularities arising from the Whitney sum, it is shown that, unlike classical tangent bundle cases, the hyperbolic frame bundle of an oriented manifold admits lifting without any topological obstruction, that is, it admits a structure of the connected double covering of $\mathrm{GL}^{+}(2m,\mathbb{R})$, and the hyperbolic tangent bundle carries a $Spin^{e}_{m,m}$ structure (with $m=\dim\mathcal{M}$), whatever the value of $w_2(\mathcal{M})$. These conclusions are known from the work of Karoubi and Gualtieri and the point of this note is that they follow from the Whitney product formula alone, or from the additivity formula of Whitney sums with an explicit covering group, without recourse to Karoubi's criterion for indefinite signature. We also describe the spinor bundles involved, which are bundles of differential forms and not Dirac spinor bundles and show that orientability is needed for the covering of the full linear group.
item.dc:creator: J. M. Hoff da Silva, E. Notte-Cuello

item.title: Thermalization with Gaussian Quantum Cellular Automata
item.description: arXiv:2606.05542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of many-body bosonic lattice systems under translation-invariant Gaussian quantum cellular automata. We formulate two sets of conditions on GQCAs which separately guarantee thermalization of any state on the local Weyl algebra to the infinite temperature state, whenever the state is locally normal and has uniformly bounded particle density. Our main intermediate result is a quantum many-body generalization of the classic Riemann-Lebesgue lemma which is a bound on expectation values of local Weyl operators involving their support and the state's particle density.
item.dc:creator: Roman Geiko, Jake Gerenraich

item.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.31189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions defined by differential recursions: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. Their rational coefficient functions produce palindromic and anti-palindromic triangles, including OEIS A336110 and A140136. For general differential order $p$, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn-type companions. An explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual generating function. The companions share a principal symbol and a rationally parametrized characteristic curve with a projective $S_3$ action. At $p=2$ this construction yields the Narayana quadratic. At $p=3$ the symmetry lifts to $S_4$: two algebraic sectors are edge resolvents of one quartic root configuration, and the nonsymmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia generating function has degree four. For $p=4$ and $p=5$ we derive algebraic equations of degrees six and eight, respectively, and find Galois groups $S_6$ and $S_8$ at generic specializations. At $p=6$ we verify a degree-ten specialization with Galois group $S_{10}$. Their discriminants exhibit a universal cubic characteristic factor and a squared lower-order factor. A boundary factorization explains the observed algebraic degrees and discriminant monomials. We formulate conjectures on algebraicity and Galois groups in the reduced hierarchy and identify a possible mechanism for transcendence in the higher self-dual hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: S. Voloshyn

item.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21268v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operator with bounded nonconstant iid potential, we prove a unit-intensity Poisson limit for local eigenvalues unfolded by the integrated density of states. The limit holds at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. In particular, it holds for Bernoulli potentials at every fixed nonzero coupling. The proof uses auxiliary phase functions built from inverse stationary measures to obtain an exact IDS drift. Projective contraction then yields exponential crossing times, and a spatial subdivision argument gives independent Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows. At energies where the IDS has a finite positive derivative, the usual linear rescaling gives the same limit.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
item.description: arXiv:2610.30542v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.
item.dc:creator: E. Notte-Cuello, J. M. Hoff da Silva

item.title: Gaussian $\beta$-Markov Path Spaces without a Spectral Gap and the Araki--Woods Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Derezi\'nski and G\'erard constructed the Gaussian $\beta$-Markov path space of a free Bose field in a form equivalent to the Araki--Woods representation, which suits nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with a quantum-field environment, but only for one-particle Hamiltonians with a spectral gap. We extend this construction, together with the equivalence to the Araki--Woods representation, to one-particle Hamiltonians without a spectral gap. The extension is intended for constructive quantum field theory at positive temperature and equilibrium statistical mechanics, for instance in the problem of the absence of Bose--Einstein condensation of quasiparticles whose number is not conserved.
item.dc:creator: Yoshitsugu Sekine

item.title: Drinfeld J Presentation of Twisted Yangians
item.description: arXiv:1401.2143v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a quantization of a Lie coideal structure for twisted half-loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebras. We obtain algebra closure relations of twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for all symmetric pairs of simple Lie algebras and for simple twisted even half-loop Lie algebras. We provide the explicit form of the closure relations for twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for the ${\mathfrak{sl}}_3$ Lie algebra.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Belliard, Vidas Regelskis

item.title: Power rate of convergence of discrete curves: framework and applications
item.description: arXiv:2407.10243v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a framework for power-law rates of convergence of random discrete curves to Schramm Loewner Evolution (SLE). We show that a power-law rate of convergence of a suitable martingale observable gives a power-law rate of convergence of the interface to SLE, provided the discrete curves satisfy the Kemppainen-Smirnov crossing condition; the proof uses known estimates on the derivative of the SLE map. We apply the framework to the exploration process of critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, obtaining a power-law rate of convergence to SLE$_6$.
item.dc:creator: Ilia Binder, Larissa Richards

item.title: Memory-Augmented Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing
item.description: arXiv:2409.09886v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) is an effective method for predicting chaotic systems by using a high-dimensional dynamic reservoir with fixed internal weights, while keeping the learning phase linear, which simplifies training and reduces computational complexity compared to fully trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses the exponential growth of Hilbert spaces in quantum systems, allowing for greater information processing, memory capacity, and computational power. However, the original QRC proposal requires coherent injection of inputs multiple times, complicating practical implementation. We present a hybrid quantum-classical approach that implements memory through classical post-processing of quantum measurements. This approach avoids the need for multiple coherent input injections and is evaluated on benchmark tasks, including the chaotic Mackey-Glass time series prediction. We tested our model on two physical platforms: a fully connected Ising model and a Rydberg atom array. The optimized model demonstrates promising predictive capabilities, achieving a higher number of steps compared to previously reported approaches.
item.dc:creator: J. Settino, L. Salatino, L. Mariani, M. Channab, L. Bozzolo, S. Vallisa, P. Barill\`a, A. Policicchio, N. Lo Gullo, A. Giordano, C. Mastroianni, F. Plastina

item.title: New exact solutions of the 3D Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2506.04725v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Previously we found a unique quantum system with a positive gauge-invariant Weyl-Stratonovich quasi-probability density function which can be defined by the so-called {\guillemotleft}quadratic funnel{\guillemotright} potential. In this work we have constructed a class of exact solutions to the 3D Schr\"odinger equation for a two-parameter {\guillemotleft}quadratic funnel{\guillemotright} potential based on the $\Psi$ -model of micro and macro systems. It should be noted that the Aharonov-Bohm effect is inherent in the quantum $\Psi$ -model. Explicit expressions for the energy spectrum and the set of eigenfunctions have been found. Using gauge invariance for scalar and vector potentials, a solution to the electromagnetic Schr\"odinger equation has been obtained, with a magnetic field in the form of a {\guillemotleft}Dirac string{\guillemotright} defined by a singular vortex probability flux field. Superpositions of eigenfunctions leading to various types of vortex and potential probability current fields have been investigated in detail. The analysis of the quantum system's properties has been carried out within the Wigner-Vlasov formalism.
item.dc:creator: E. E. Perepelkin, B. I. Sadovnikov, N. G. Inozemtseva, A. S. Medvedev

item.title: Accessing Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard equations in a nonlinear framework of quantum mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2602.04747v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we present the reduction of a recently introduced generalized quantum scheme of Chodos and Cooper to Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard classes of nonlinear system that enable us to furnish a wider class of acceptable solutions. In particular, for the Levinson-Smith equations, we find their relevance to position-dependent mass quantum systems, with an interesting off-shoot that solitonic-like solutions emerge from the condition of the level surface in the system. On the other hand, for the Li\'{e}nard type, which has coefficients of odd and odd symmetry in the present set up, we demonstrate that closed form solutions exist on carrying out conversion to the typical Abel form.
item.dc:creator: Bijan Bagchi, Anindya Ghose-Choudhury

item.title: GAP Measures and Wave Function Collapse
item.description: arXiv:2602.19993v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: GAP measures (also known as Scrooge measures) are a natural class of probability distributions on the unit sphere of a Hilbert space that come up in quantum statistical mechanics; for each density matrix $\rho$ there is a unique measure GAP$_\rho$. We describe and prove a property of these measures that was not recognized so far: If a wave function $\Psi$ is GAP$_\rho$ distributed and a collapse occurs, then the collapsed wave function $\Psi'$ is again GAP distributed (relative to the appropriate $\rho'$). This fact applies to collapses due to a quantum measurement carried out by an observer, as well as to spontaneous collapse theories such as CSL or GRW. More precisely, it is the conditional distribution of $\Psi'$, given the measurement outcome (respectively, the noise in CSL or the collapse history in GRW), that is GAP$_{\rho'}$.
item.dc:creator: Roderich Tumulka

item.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and non-Markovianity: a collisional model perspective
item.description: arXiv:2603.14015v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accessing the physical mechanisms behind non-Markovian phenomena in open quantum dynamics requires the study of the statistical properties of the joint system-environment dynamics. This is impossible at the level of the reduced dynamics of the open system alone as the latter is obtained by suitably eliminating the environment. The task is instead made possible by considering multi-time correlation functions involving observables of the open system, only: the open system-environment interactions turn them into global ones thus building up correlations between the two systems. Multi-time correlations form the basis of both the theory of quantum stochastic processes and of the Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical entropy (ALF entropy for short). This latter quantity provides for quantum systems a measure of the dynamical entropy production as the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy does for classical systems. In the case of a collisional model whereby the dissipative dynamics of a finite-level system is obtained by its coupling to an infinite classical spin chain, the ALF entropy can be explicitly computed. It turns out to depend on the parameters characterizing the statistical properties of the environment and can be related to the activation and super-activation of memory effects in the open quantum system.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Nichele, Fabio Benatti

item.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and Dissipative Information Flows
item.description: arXiv:2603.14025v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical (ALF) entropy measures the rate at which new information is gathered about a quantum system by inspecting its long-time evolution. We propose an extension of the ALF entropy to open quantum dynamics as a measure of back-flow of information from the environment. Such a proposal is stronger than the existing ones based only on the open system reduced dynamics. In the case of a qubit collisionally coupled to a classical spin chain, we obtain an exact expression for the $\textit{open-system ALF entropy}$ explicitly depending on the environment correlations. An extreme case shows how the information flow from environment to system corresponds to vanishing entropy production as for reversible finite quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Nichele, Fabio Benatti

item.title: Reconstruction of F-cohomological field theories on moduli of compact type
item.description: arXiv:2604.07270v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an analogue of Givental-Teleman reconstruction for F-cohomological field theories on the moduli space of compact type. We apply it to reconstruct the restriction of the extended $r$-spin classes to the extended direction and deduce relations between $\kappa$-classes (both in compact type).
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, Silvia Ragni, Paolo Rossi

item.title: Eigenvalue formulation of Stochastic Inflation and application to large perturbation generating inflationary features
item.description: arXiv:2606.00176v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stochastic inflation is a powerful technique for calculating the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations, which may collapse to form Primordial Black Holes. The PDF, $P({\cal N})$, of the stochastic number of e-folds, ${\cal N}$, satisfies an adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation. We develop a new self-contained eigenvalue technique which can be used to determine $P({\cal N})$. First we apply this method to the simple case of quantum diffusion along a flat potential without any classical drift. We recover the expression for the PDF that has previously been found using characteristic functions, with an exponential tail, and a power-law behaviour, $P({\cal N}) \propto {\cal N}^{-3/2}$, in the intermediate regime between the peak and the tail of the PDF. Finally we apply the method to constant drift inflation, in the narrow- and broad-well limits. In the narrow-well limit, there is an analytic solution and the PDF is similar to the drift-free case, with a mildly suppressed tail. In the broad-well limit, determining the full set of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions requires a piecewise construction of the spectrum, and the broad-well PDF is qualitatively different, with an enhanced peak and a strongly suppressed tail.

item.title: Isotropic random walks and Brownian diffusion on complex projective space
item.description: arXiv:2606.11438v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study isotropic random walks on complex projective space in the context of stochastic state-space exploration in open quantum systems. Using results from harmonic analysis on compact rank-one symmetric spaces, first we obtain explicit transition kernels and characterise the evolution of fidelity and geometric observables. Then, we establish the correspondence between the small-step limit and Fubini-Study Brownian motion, and also show that the long-time limit reproduces Haar-random state statistics. At the level of the density matrix, the ensemble evolution formally coincides with an isotropic depolarizing channel at all times. Our main results concern first-passage statistics to high-fidelity target states. In the Brownian limit, we derive a closed-form expression for the mean first-passage time and an explicit spectral representation of the first-passage-time distribution, with decay rates determined by the eigenvalues of the killed Fubini-Study Laplace-Beltrami operator. The resulting asymptotics reveal a strong dependence on target fidelity and Hilbert-space dimension, demonstrating the rapidly increasing difficulty of reaching high-fidelity targets through unbiased isotropic exploration. The model is purely geometric and does not incorporate microscopic Hamiltonians or Lindblad dynamics. Nevertheless, the results suggest that it offers a natural starting point for stochastic models of open quantum systems that incorporate Hamiltonian and dissipative effects, with potential applications to stochastic quantum state preparation and control.
item.dc:creator: Gyula I. T\'oth

item.title: Symbol sequences from three-rotor coincidences and their word-complexity
item.description: arXiv:2606.25766v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the three-rotor problem, three equally massive point particles move on a circle interacting via attractive pairwise cosine potentials. Rotors can represent superconducting phases of metallic segments in a chain of coupled Josephson junctions. We propose a digitization of the classical dynamics that records successive pair and triple coincidences of rotors using four symbols. Rotor coincidences correspond to boundaries in a disjoint partition of the configuration torus into cells where the rotors are ordered clockwise and anticlockwise. It is shown that isolated rotor coincidences must be crossings. Despite being a rather coarse digitization, we find that replacing trajectories by coincidence symbol sequences captures significant qualitative features of the dynamics through word statistics. Word-complexity $C_n$ measures the diversity of $n$-letter words in the symbol sequence while topological entropy governs asymptotic exponential growth of $C_n$. Sequences from periodic orbits have a word-complexity that saturates at the period. Ultra-high-energy trajectories with irrational `slope' are quasiperiodic. We show that they have zero entropy and $C_n = n+3$ by examining limiting slopes and by a mapping to Sturmian sequences. We examine their grammar rules and propose how their right-special words may be identified. On the other hand, numerical investigation of sequences from globally chaotic orbits leads us to conjecture an exponentially growing word-complexity $C_n = 3 \times 2^{n-1}$ with a topological entropy $\log 2$. We identify grammar rules that imply this conjectured word-complexity and model the resulting sequences as a subshift of finite type, unlike those at ultra-high energies which are not topological Markov chains.
item.dc:creator: Govind S. Krishnaswami, Anirudh Rameshan

item.title: A Single Physical Principle Determines Quantum Relative Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2607.01712v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Why does quantum relative entropy occupy such a privileged role among measures of distinguishability? We show that a single operational principle determines it. If one pair of states can be distinguished at least as successfully as another for every prior, when both are assisted by the same auxiliary pair, acting as a catalyst, a distinguishability measure should assign it no smaller value. Remarkably, for a normalized measure, this requirement singles out Umegaki relative entropy under mild classical continuity and expansibility on uniform distributions: adding impossible outcomes leaves their associated entropy unchanged. Qubit catalysts already suffice. No additivity or quantum continuity is assumed. We also prove that, without auxiliary assistance, respecting binary discrimination dominance uniquely determines the quantum extension of every regular classical divergence, including the Hirche--Tomamichel extensions of classical $f$-divergences. For additive classical divergences, these extensions respect classical catalysis; allowing noncommuting qubit catalysts is what singles out Umegaki relative entropy.
item.dc:creator: Gilad Gour

item.title: Symmetries and Conservation Laws in Lie-Poisson Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.04522v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lie-Poisson electrodynamics (LPE) is a non-Abelian and nonlinear deformation of usual electrodynamics, where the gauge algebra is defined through a Lie-algebra-type Poisson bracket on space-time. This field-theoretical model arises from noncommutative U(1) gauge theory in the semiclassical limit. We focus on the geometric approach to LPE in the absence of charged matter. We establish a non-trivial field redefinition which, under mild technical assumptions, maps the LPE dynamics to that of Maxwell theory. We emphasise that despite the dynamical equivalence, these two theories are not physically equivalent, since the corresponding local gauge-invariant observables are different. We show that our field redefinition is actually a Seiberg-Witten map between LPE and Maxwell theory. Using this map, for any symmetry of the Maxwell action, we construct generators of LPE symmetries and the corresponding conserved currents. In particular, we obtain deformed Poincar\'e transformations, thereby solving the problem of constructing space-time symmetries in LPE. The deformed symmetries are constructed as active transformations of the gauge field. In the outlook, we propose a natural quantization prescription for LPE based on our field redefinition.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Kurkov

item.title: Relativistic transport near moving interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.28569v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study linear disturbances localized near planar surfaces moving at constant velocity $v$ in relativistic media. Depending on the physical setting, the surface may represent a moving obstacle, a thermal boundary, or an external source, providing a unified description of boundary layers, wakes, and the asymptotic tails of shock waves. The central result is a propagator representation of the interface solution that yields a geometric characterization of these phenomena. Using a Laplace-transform formulation, we show that the solution is a superposition of modes with purely imaginary frequency and wavenumber. For a given interface velocity, the admissible modes are selected by the line $i\omega=vik$ in the $\{i\omega,ik\}$ plane. As $v$ varies, this line sweeps across the spectrum, providing a unified geometric description of interface-localized solutions for arbitrary interface velocities. We illustrate the formalism with applications to relativistic hydrodynamics and kinetic theory.
