item.title: Long-Time Dispersion and Threshold Resonances for the Landau Hamiltonian on the Hyperbolic Plane
item.description: arXiv:2609.12999v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A uniform magnetic field completely suppresses long-time dispersion for the Euclidean Landau Hamiltonian. We show that negative curvature fundamentally changes this behavior. For the Landau Hamiltonian with arbitrary field strength $B\in\mathbb R$ on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb H$, we establish sharp dispersive estimates for the Schr\"odinger evolution on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace. The decay is $|t|^{-1}$ at short times and, strikingly, improves to $|t|^{-3/2}$ at large times whenever $B\notin\frac12+\mathbb Z$. At half-integer fields, we identify a threshold resonance and isolate its leading contribution, which yields the slower but sharp rate $|t|^{-1/2}$. Thus the long-time dynamics exhibit a resonance-driven dichotomy with no analogue in the flat constant-field problem. Our analysis is based on an explicit representation of the magnetic Schr\"odinger kernel together with a precise separation of the Landau levels and threshold profile. As a further consequence, for every nonthreshold field we obtain global-in-time Strichartz estimates on the absolutely continuous spectral subspace throughout the full hyperbolic admissible region.
item.dc:creator: Huanqing Guo, Haoran Wang, Junyong Zhang, Jiqiang Zheng

item.title: A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2609.19280v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Faster quantum gates can reduce the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors, speeding up gates often involves stronger microwave pulses, which can increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that gate transition rates at fixed trace distance between the initial and final system states grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under pulse-uniformity conditions, without assuming an upper bound on the coupling strength. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Restrepo Gaviria, Mischa P. Woods

item.title: Sharp Riesz capacity inequalities and the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.04811v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $n\geq2$ and $p\in(n-2,n)$, we prove that closed balls maximize the ratio of Riesz $p$-capacity to Newtonian capacity among all compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. This resolves the classical P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} capacity ratio conjecture and its higher-dimensional extensions. For $n\geq4$, a sharp inequality for the ratio of Newtonian capacity to logarithmic capacity is established. All equality cases are characterized.
item.dc:creator: Mengwei Su, Qiang Sun, Ge Xiong

item.title: Approximation of a continuous-variable Gaussian state by discrete-variable quantum states
item.description: arXiv:2610.05623v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every centered one-mode continuous-variable Gaussian state, we prove that the signed Wigner periodization defines a discrete-variable density operator in every odd dimension $d\ge3$. Positivity is equivalent to the one-mode uncertainty condition, and we determine the complete inertia outside and on its boundary. A covariance-independent isometric embedding gives exponential convergence in trace norm, with an explicit error bound uniform in Planck's constant. For covariance twice the identity, dimension $31$ gives a certified trace-norm error below $1/8000$. The trace-norm estimate controls all measurement probabilities. We retain the original canonical-coherent-frame formula in terms of the determinant and trace of the covariance matrix, with continuous normalization fixed to agree with the discrete frame convention. The coherence comparisons identify which diagnostics accompany the controlled state approximation. Position- and momentum-basis coherences have exponentially convergent values after division by the square root of the dimension. Numerical comparisons of purity and frame coherence illustrate the discrete-continuous transition.
item.dc:creator: Nicolae Cotfas, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
item.description: arXiv:2610.05953v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model is a strongly interacting fermionic system. Its dynamics are difficult to analyze with Lieb-Robinson bounds and cluster expansions due to its all-to-all disordered interactions. We prove that, with high probability over the disorder, the SYK model admits a quantum Gibbs sampler with a system-size-independent spectral gap at sufficiently high constant temperatures. This yields polynomial-time preparation of SYK Gibbs states on a quantum computer. While prior non-rigorous computations that suggested SYK thermalization were limited to studying local correlators, we emphasize that our result holds up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance. Our proof introduces the pseudo-Lindbladian approach to fermions then applies two key new ideas: a Bochner inequality for quantum dynamics, and an especially simple SYK analysis based on a comparison to classical dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yiyi Cai, Yongtao Zhan, Alexander Zlokapa

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe equations of the form $i\partial_tu+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. Under the additional assumption $e\neq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. Unlike the previous $H^1$ global theory based on Takaoka's periodic well-posedness estimates (2000), our result does not require any non-resonance condition on the coefficients. Our approach relies on the construction of modified higher-order energies, following the strategy developed for the generalized KdV equation by Planchon, Tzvetkov and Visciglia (2023) and for the generalized DNLS equation by Hayashi, Ozawa and Visciglia (2025). Motivated by higher-order modulation theory, we exploit the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow to establish Sobolev bounds uniform in the modulation parameter $\varepsilon$ on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$. This corresponds to physical times of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$, which is the natural time scale anticipated for the NLS-Dysthe approximation.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani

item.title: Almost-optimal bulk regularity conditions in the CLT for G$\beta$E
item.description: arXiv:2610.24211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider linear statistics $\sum_{k=1}^N f(x_k)$ of a Gaussian $\b$-ensemble. Following the work of \cite{LaSo22}, which was concerned only with Wigner matrices, we extend their results for general $\b$. In particular, we show that the CLT holds for any $f \in H^{1/2 + \e}$. The novel input which was not used in \cite{LaSo22} is the Helffer-Sj\"ostrand representation for the covariance, first appearing the random matrix context in \cite{ErYa15}, coupled with characteristic flow estimates for DBM, first appearing in \cite{Bo22}.
item.dc:creator: Albert Zhang

item.title: Marginal bunching for \textit{in situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability
item.description: arXiv:2610.25471v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose an \textit{in situ} method for certifying the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in generic linear interferometers. For particles occupying distinct input ports, the method uses two-particle marginal bunching or anti-bunching probabilities to bound full multiparticle indistinguishability through Aldous' spectral gap theorem. For Haar-random unitary interferometers, the number of experimental runs required to estimate this bound to a prescribed precision, at fixed confidence, is polynomial in the particle number, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability over the choice of interferometer. Losses are incorporated without conditioning on particle survival. The method is particularly suited to certifying photon indistinguishability in large-scale interference experiments, including Boson Sampling experiments targeting quantum computational advantage.
item.dc:creator: Valery Shchesnovich

item.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.34240v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\RR^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple $\U(1)$ model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an $\SU(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali

item.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.35918v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility throughout the parameter family and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yisong Yang

item.title: Zero-freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
item.description: arXiv:2610.40510v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study antiferromagnetic spin systems on random regular graphs through the lens of the phase transitions characterized by the complex zeros of the partition function. Our motivating examples include the hardcore model and the antiferromagnetic Potts model (including proper $q$-colorings at $\beta=0$). For both models on random $d$-regular graphs, we establish, with high probability over the graph, zero-free regions throughout the interior of the replica-symmetric regime. Asymptotically, this regime extends up to tree occupation density $$\alpha < \alpha_{\mathrm{RSB}}(d) = (2\log d - 2\log\log d + 2 - 2\log 2 + o_d(1))/d$$ for the hardcore model and up to degree $$d < d_{\mathrm{RSB}}(q) = (2q-1)\log q - 2\log 2 + o_q(1)$$ for proper $q$-colorings. Leveraging the standard algorithmic implications of zero-freeness, we obtain deterministic polynomial-time algorithms that multiplicatively approximate the corresponding partition functions at fixed rational parameters throughout this regime, with high probability over the graph. Our algorithmic guarantees significantly improve upon prior work and extend beyond the parameter ranges reached by previously known search algorithms. As a key intermediate step, we establish the pointwise equivalence, away from the threshold, of three notions of replica symmetry: geometric (averaged pairwise correlation decay), thermodynamic (convergence to the Bethe free-energy prediction), and variational (nonpositivity of the Bethe functional). To establish zero-freeness, we develop reinforced small subgraph conditioning, lifting classical small subgraph conditioning to random holomorphic functions to control short-cycle fluctuations. We also use variational replica symmetry to obtain exponential planted overlap concentration. This enables a typical-graph truncation that controls complex second moments up to the replica symmetry breaking threshold.
item.dc:creator: Zejia Chen, Chunyang Wang, Xinyuan Zhang

item.title: Spectral Theory and Continuum Norm Resolvent Convergence of a One-Sided Discrete Dirac-Type Operator
item.description: arXiv:2611.00820v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a one-dimensional discrete Dirac-type operator $D_d$ acting on the Hilbert space $\big(\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$, obtained from the classical continuous free Dirac operator by replacing the spatial derivative with the one-sided backward difference operator $I - S_1$, where $S_1$ denotes the right shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})$. We establish the fundamental operator-theoretic and spectral properties of $D_d$: unlike symmetric or supersymmetric lattice discretizations, $D_d$ is bounded and non-normal for every non-zero rest mass $m > 0$, with self-commutator $[D_d, D_d^\dag] = -2mc^3(-\Delta_{\mathrm{disc}})\sigma_2$, yet it is quadratically normal. We compute the exact operator norm, determine the exact spectral radius in two mass regimes, and show via Fourier--Laurent analysis that the spectrum $\sigma(D_d)$ is purely continuous and lies on a two-component algebraic curve in the complex plane undergoing a topological transition at $mc^2 = 2c$. Finally, introducing a lattice spacing $h > 0$ and embedding $\big(\ell^2(h\mathbb{Z};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ isometrically into $\big(L^2(\mathbb{R};\mathbb{C})\big)^2$ via Whittaker--Shannon band-limited interpolation, we prove that the scaled non-normal discrete Dirac-type operator $D_{d,h}$ converges to the continuous self-adjoint Dirac operator $D$ in the norm resolvent sense at the optimal rate $\mathcal{O}(h)$ as $h \to 0^+$, without requiring frequency cutoffs.
item.dc:creator: Mariusz Niwi\'nski

item.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.02070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.
